title: No spectrally minimal graph of order 2k with matching number k lies in Hou and Tan's family T'_{2k,k}
summary: Hou and Tan's Construction 9 gives no tree of order 2k for k ≥ 3, so their question whether every spectrally minimal graph with matching number k lies in T'_{n,k} has a negative answer at the boundary n = 2k; Lean checks the degree count, and the range n ≥ 2k+1 stays open.
abstract: Let G_{n,k} be the family of connected graphs of order n with matching number k. Hou and Tan (arXiv:2607.11061v2) proved a sharp lower bound for the spectral radius on G_{n,k}. For general n ≥ 2k they defined a family T'_{n,k} of trees (Construction 9) and asked: for arbitrary n and k, must every spectrally minimal graph in G_{n,k} belong to T'_{n,k}? We show that the answer to this question, as written in arXiv v2, is no. The failure is at the boundary n = 2k of the range of the construction. For every k ≥ 3, Construction 9 with n = 2k gives no tree of order 2k: each tree that it builds has at least 2k+1 vertices. The path P_{2k} is in G_{2k,k}, so G_{2k,k} has spectrally minimal graphs, and none of them is in T'_{2k,k}. The proof is a short degree count. Lean 4 with Mathlib checks the counting step for all k ≥ 3, with only the standard axioms; the facts about P_{2k} are elementary and are checked by hand and by computer for small k. The result does not touch the range n ≥ 2k+1. There, a floating-point search over all trees of order at most 20 finds every spectrally minimal graph in T'_{n,k} (90 pairs (n,k)), so the question restricted to n ≥ 2k+1 stays open. We did not read the journal version of the source paper (Linear Algebra Appl. 755 (2027)), so we do not know if its text has the same range. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The computations, the proofs and the text were produced by AI models (from Anthropic and OpenAI), working under the author's direction.
